title: Compact reauth helpers and typed stream adapters to align ergonomics across Python/TypeScript/Go
author: Asha Mirza
description: Motivation: SDK users reported repeated friction when reauthorizing long-lived streaming sessions and when migrating examples across languages. This PR introduces a compact set of reauth helpers and small typed stream adapter layers for Python, TypeScript, and Go to achieve API ergonomics parity and reduce boilerplate. Goals: 1) Provide a minimal "credential refresher" helper that can be composed into existing stream connectors; 2) Add lightweight typed stream adapters that expose a consistent async-iterator/pull-stream surface across languages; 3) Reduce duplication in examples and make cross-language migration straightforward; 4) Bump TypeScript and Go SDK patch versions to include the adapter and helper packages. High level changes: - Py: package redwood_sdk.streaming.reauth with CredentialLease and refresh callback shim; new examples in examples/streaming/reauth_demo.py. - TS: introduce @redwood/sdk-helpers/reauth and stream-adapter async generator wrapper; update ts-sdk readme examples. - Go: add compact cred.Refresher interface and stream/adapter package with typed channel-backed iterator; small concurrency guard to avoid double-refresh. - Cross-lang: harmonize env var names and docs snippets (REDWOOD_TOKEN_TTL_HINT). Compatibility: default behavior is backward compatible; helpers are opt-in. We added a low-overhead heartbeat/lease check that will attempt reauth only when TTL drops below threshold. This PR intentionally avoids a global credential cache to keep surface area small and deterministic for Dedicated/Private deployments.
commits: 1) feat(ts): add reauth helper and typed stream adapter (ts/helpers/*) ; 2) feat(py): add CredentialLease shim and examples (py/redwood_sdk/streaming/reauth.py) ; 3) feat(go): introduce cred.Refresher and stream/adapter (go/sdk/cred, go/sdk/stream/adapter) ; 4) docs: cross-language examples and migration guide ; 5) chore: bump ts/sdk to 1.13.2, go/sdk to v0.9.7, py SDK to 2.8.4 ; 6) fix: race in go refresher backoff logic (follow-up commit)
diff_summary: Small to medium: add helper modules in each SDK, a couple of example files, docs page, and version bumps. No changes to runtime or server-side code. Tests: new unit tests for reauth logic (py/ts/go), integration smoke test updated to exercise a credential lease refresh path.
review_comments: Diego: requested clarity on backoff config and a test for simultaneous refresh requests; Claire: asked for clearer example of how this behaves under Dedicated reserved capacity; Owen: pointed out a potential panic in go channel iterator when consumer cancels mid-refresh. Author addressed all requests: added backoff config struct with defaults, added Python and TS unit tests for concurrent refresh, fixed go panic by adding a non-blocking select and close-safety guard. Final approvals from Diego and Claire on 2026-03-04.
ci_checks: Unit: pass; Integration-smoke: pass (flaky windows runner retried once); Lint: pass; Typecheck(ts): pass; Go vet: pass; Py static typing: pass
release_notes: Added compact credential refresher helpers and typed stream adapters across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Opt-in helpers simplify reauth logic for long-lived streams; examples and migration guide included. Bumped Py SDK to 2.8.4, TS SDK to 1.13.2, Go SDK to v0.9.7.
notes_for_consumers: How to adopt: - Minimal: import the helper and pass a small refresh callback that exchanges your rotated secret for a token; - Migration: replace your ad-hoc token refresh loops with CredentialLease / Refresher for predictable TTL checks; - Performance: the helper checks TTL every 10% of token lifetime by default and will only attempt refresh once per lease window. - Dedicated: no changes required to server config; helpers are client-side only.
testing_notes: Added unit tests covering: credential TTL check edge cases, concurrent refresh dedupe, stream adapter order preservation, and graceful consumer cancellation. Ran full sdk test matrix on linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. Observed a transient timing flake in the TS generator under heavy load; added a small jitter to the retry timer to mitigate.
maintainer_guidance: This change is low-risk and intended to be backwards compatible. If downstream code uses an internal credential cache, recommend a staged rollout and verify behavior in Dedicated staging. Monitor token-refresh-related errors (tag: sdk.cred.refresh.fail) and streaming reconnects (tag: sdk.stream.reconnect) for first week after release. If needed, revert is simple by removing helper imports; behavior falls back to previous explicit refresh loops.
